locations.setting: Two disused brick water reservoirs from 1872 on Zluty kopec hill in Brno, joined later by two concrete tanks, decommissioned in 1997 and now toured as cavernous underground chambers.

locations.name: Vojna Memorial
locations.setting: An intact forced-labour camp near Pribram built in 1947-49 for uranium mining and later a political prison until 1960, preserved with its command building, bunker and unheated punishment cells.
locations.known_for: Zdivocela zeme, Bumerang, Piknik, Nackt unter Wolfen

locations.name: Vonwiller Factory, Zamberk
locations.setting: A former 1838 textile mill on the edge of Zamberk, now a museum of antique machinery and vehicles, with a working line-shaft machine shop, forge, narrow-gauge railway and a stock of vintage cars.
locations.facilities: Functional line-shaft machine shop with over 30 machines, forge, narrow-gauge railway, vintage car and motorcycle collection, restoration workshop

locations.name: Winternitz Villa
locations.setting: 1932 house in Prague's Smíchov district designed by Adolf Loos around his raumplan of interlocking split levels, now a museum open for tours and filming by appointment.

locations.name: Zabrdovice Municipal Baths, Brno
locations.setting: A 1932 Bohuslav Fuchs bathing complex in Brno's Zabrdovice district built around two courtyards, its outdoor pool still operating as a public lido while the closed indoor winter baths await reuse.

locations.name: Zbrojovka, Brno
locations.setting: The former Czechoslovak state arms works in Brno's Husovice district, founded in 1918, which also repaired cars and rail equipment and made weapons before its 1945 machinery seeded the Zetor tractor brand.

locations.name: Zlín Factory Complex
locations.setting: Grid of red brick functionalist factory halls built by the Baťa shoe company in Zlín from the 1920s, now reused as a university, offices and cultural venues.

locations.name: Bakken (Dyrehavsbakken)
locations.setting: An amusement park dating to 1583 inside the Jaegersborg Dyrehave deer park north of Copenhagen, with rides, variety theatres and restaurants under old beech trees.
locations.suitability: Hosts company events and group bookings (own site: 'Firmaarrangementer')

locations.name: Bella Center
locations.setting: Scandinavia's second-largest exhibition and conference centre in Copenhagen's Orestad district, with a congress hall for up to 4,200 people, four auditoriums and an adjoining hotel tower.
locations.known_for: Olsen-banden ser rodt (The Olsen Gang Outta Sight)

locations.name: Bornholm Airport
locations.setting: Regional airport near Roenne on Bornholm with scheduled flights to Copenhagen, Aalborg, Billund and Sonderborg, the island's only air link.

locations.name: Carlsberg Byen
locations.setting: Former Carlsberg brewery grounds in Copenhagen, redeveloped into a city district that keeps historic brewery halls and towers alongside new office, retail and residential buildings.

locations.name: Christiansborg Palace
locations.setting: Government palace on the Slotsholmen islet housing the Danish Parliament, Prime Minister's Office and Supreme Court, with a riding ground complex and palace square.
locations.suitability: The palace's manager, the Royal Danish Collection, states it welcomes press inquiries, including for TV shows, and that holders of valid press credentials get free admission to any of its palaces without advance booking (contact via the Head of Communications).

locations.name: Cirkusbygningen
locations.setting: A domed circus building from 1886 in central Copenhagen near Tivoli, its ring and tiered seating now hired out for shows, dinner theatre and events.
locations.suitability: Building available for hire for events (own site: 'Lej bygningen til dit event')

locations.name: Copenhagen City Hall
locations.setting: The seat of Copenhagen's municipal government on Radhuspladsen, a National Romantic building from 1905 with a public atrium and clock tower, used for a tower scene in a 1978 comedy and for hospital-atrium scenes in a 2015 drama.
locations.known_for: The Olsen Gang Goes to War, The Danish Girl

locations.name: Copenhagen Police Headquarters (Politigarden)
locations.setting: A 1924 neoclassical police headquarters in central Copenhagen built around a 45-metre circular courtyard with 44 Doric columns, still an active police building, that has repeatedly played itself on screen.
locations.known_for: Broen/Bron (The Bridge), Forbrydelsen (The Killing), Olsen-banden films

locations.name: CopenHill (Amager Bakke)
locations.setting: Working waste-to-energy plant in Copenhagen with a rooftop ski slope, climbing wall and hiking trail built onto its sloped roof, plus a rooftop bar and cafe.
locations.facilities: Rooftop bar and event space, cafe, elevator access to the roof

locations.name: Dokk1
locations.setting: A large glass and concrete public library and citizen service building on Aarhus harbourfront, with open multi-storey interiors and a public square outside.

locations.name: DR Byen
locations.setting: The headquarters and production complex of the Danish Broadcasting Corporation on Amager, opened between 2006 and 2010, combining newsrooms, TV studios and the DR Koncerthuset concert hall.

locations.name: DR Koncerthuset
locations.setting: Concert hall in Copenhagen's Orestad district built for Danish public broadcaster DR, with a main concert hall, four recording studios and a restaurant, available for external hire.
locations.facilities: Concert hall, four recording studios, external hire for concerts and conferences

locations.name: FAENGSLET (Horsens State Prison)
locations.setting: Former Danish state prison in Horsens, closed in 2006 and reopened as a prison museum whose cell wings, exercise yards and workshop buildings are hired out for events and overnight stays.
locations.facilities: Cell wings, museum halls, conference and event spaces, overnight accommodation

locations.name: Filmby Aarhus
locations.setting: Creative business park in Aarhus's Sydhavnen district housing over 80 film, TV, gaming and animation companies, with production premises and an event bar for hire.
locations.facilities: Rental of commercial premises and production facilities, event bar

locations.name: Filmbyen
locations.setting: A production complex of offices, sound stages, edit suites and filmmaker pavilions built inside a former military barracks in Avedore, headquarters of Zentropa and home to several other Danish production companies.

locations.name: Gammel Estrup
locations.setting: Renaissance manor house in Jutland, home to Denmark's national museum of manor life, with period rooms, stables, a moat and surrounding parkland used for events.

locations.name: Godsbanen
locations.setting: A former railway goods yard in Aarhus converted into a production house for culture and the arts, with its long brick freight sheds and tracks-side hall available to rent for events.
locations.suitability: Rooms and halls for hire for events (own site: 'Lej lokaler og skab events')

locations.name: H.C. Andersens Hus
locations.setting: A museum in Odense's old town dedicated to Hans Christian Andersen, combining a modern underground exhibition building with the historic house and courtyard where he was born.

locations.name: Hotel Koldingfjord
locations.setting: A former sanatorium turned hotel and conference centre on the shore of Kolding Fjord, with period interiors, function rooms and parkland running down to the water.

photo.author: FaceMePLS from The Hague, The Netherlands

locations.name: Kronborg Castle
locations.setting: Renaissance fortress at the narrowest point of the Øresund strait, with ramparts, a large courtyard and vaulted casemates, known as the Elsinore of Shakespeare's Hamlet.

locations.name: MCH Messecenter Herning
locations.setting: Denmark's largest exhibition and entertainment complex, spread across roughly 130 acres in Herning with halls used for trade fairs, concerts, sport and stage productions.

locations.name: Moens Klint (GeoCenter)
locations.setting: White chalk cliffs on the island of Moen rising up to 128 metres above the Baltic Sea, with a science centre, forest trails and beach access at the cliff base.
locations.suitability: Group bookings, guided tours and business/school event hosting

locations.name: Musikhuset Aarhus
locations.setting: A concert and performance complex in central Aarhus with ten stages under one glass-fronted roof, hosting everything from opera and classical concerts to comedy and family theatre.

locations.name: Nordisk Film Studios
locations.setting: Working studio lot in Valby founded in 1906, the world's oldest continuously active film studio, with shooting stages, post-production facilities and a 360-degree LED stage.
locations.facilities: 360-degree LED stage of 16 m diameter and 5.5 m height with LED walls and ceiling and an optional LED floor (ROE panels, up to 6,000 nits), run by Nordisk Film Shortcut; dressing rooms, makeup facilities and large parking for crew and grip trucks.
locations.suitability: The LED stage is offered for films, series, commercials, music videos and live events with virtual production supervision, Unreal Engine content, previs and driving plates; it takes vehicles, boats and planes up to 15 m. The stage runs on solar power from 2023.
locations.logistics: Mosedalvej 14, 2500 Valby, on the Nordisk Film lot; large parking for crew and grip trucks.

locations.name: Nordkraft
locations.setting: Former coal-fired power station on Aalborg's harbour front converted into a culture house, with theatre, music and exhibition halls inside the original turbine building.
locations.price_note: Commercial photography in shared areas from DKK 1,000 (about EUR 134) per day (own site)

locations.name: Nyboder
locations.setting: A historic grid of yellow single-storey row houses in central Copenhagen built from 1631 as Royal Danish Navy housing and still partly used as service housing, with a street used for a home-visit scene in a 2015 drama.

locations.name: Odense Havn
locations.setting: Commercial port on Funen with 3.9 kilometres of quay, heavy-lift cranes and large storage areas, used for offshore wind component handling and industrial tenants.
locations.facilities: Industrial space and quay for lease, heavy-load area, crane operations up to 1,200 tonnes

locations.name: Oresund Bridge
locations.setting: A cable-stayed rail and motorway bridge running nearly 8 kilometres from the Swedish coast to the artificial island of Peberholm, continuing to Denmark via the Oresund Tunnel.

locations.name: Refshaleøen
locations.setting: Former B&W shipyard peninsula in Copenhagen harbour, its industrial sheds, open dock space and workshop halls now let out for events, studios and small businesses.
locations.facilities: Industrial halls, open quay and dock space, event venues for hire

locations.name: Roskilde Cathedral
locations.setting: Brick cathedral in Roskilde and UNESCO World Heritage site, burial church of the Danish monarchy for over 500 years, with regular organ concerts and cultural events.

photo.author: CucombreLibre from New York, NY, USA

locations.name: Tivoli Gardens
locations.setting: Amusement park and pleasure garden in central Copenhagen dating from 1843, with rides, concert stages, themed architecture and landscaped gardens.
locations.facilities: Event and meeting spaces named on the business site include Nimb, Axelborgsalen and Kilden i Haven.

locations.name: Torvehallerne
locations.setting: Two glass-roofed market halls in central Copenhagen with food and drink stalls under one enclosed roof, plus an adjoining public square outside for exterior coverage.

locations.name: Utzon Center
locations.setting: Waterfront exhibition and knowledge centre in Aalborg designed by architect Jorn Utzon as his last work, with gallery halls, a restaurant and rooms available for hire.
locations.facilities: Room hire and booking, on-site restaurant

locations.name: Vridslose Prison (Vridsloeselille Faengsel)
locations.setting: A closed state prison in Albertslund built in 1859 and shut in 2018, its walled complex of cell blocks and a main gatehouse still standing at the edge of the town.

locations.name: Cable Factory (Kaapelitehdas)
locations.setting: Former Nokia cable factory in Helsinki's Ruoholahti district, a long brick industrial building with high factory halls, now a large cultural centre housing museums, studios, galleries and rentable event spaces.
locations.facilities: Dedicated space-for-rent pages for event and studio hire within the former factory halls.
locations.logistics: Managed by Kiinteistö Oy Kaapelitalo; member of the Trans Europe Halles network of industrial cultural venues.

locations.name: Finlayson Area
locations.setting: Former cotton mill founded in 1820 beside the Tammerkoski rapids in Tampere, a complex of red-brick factory buildings including the 1877 Plevna weaving hall, now holding restaurants, a cinema, shops and offices.
locations.facilities: About 80,000 sq m of rentable space across the former factory buildings; individual premises range from about 10 sq m to several thousand sq m. The buildings hold the BREEAM In-Use environmental certificate.

locations.name: Hatanpaa Manor
locations.setting: A manor house on the shore of Lake Pyhajarvi close to central Tampere, set in an English-style park with rose gardens and on-site parking for about 20 cars.

locations.name: Haveri Mine
locations.setting: A former iron and gold mine near Ylojarvi, closed in 1960 and since flooded to form a deep, clear water-filled pit now used as a dive site.

locations.name: Helsinki Olympic Stadium
locations.setting: Functionalist 1938 stadium built for the 1952 Olympics, with a 72-metre tower and a renovated bowl used today for athletics, concerts, conferences and stadium tours.
locations.facilities: Meeting rooms, restaurant, seated event spaces and a rentable tower with panoramic views.

locations.name: Hiedanranta Area
locations.setting: A former pulp and paper mill site on Tampere's lakeshore, now repurposed as a mixed venue for arts, culture and research while redevelopment of the wider area continues.

locations.name: Ivalo
locations.setting: Village on the Ivalo River about 250 kilometres north of the Arctic Circle, surrounded by boreal forest and fells, with deep snow and polar night for much of the year.

locations.name: Kehräsaari
locations.setting: Former needle factory and wool mill on a small island in central Tampere, its 1897 red-brick U-shaped building now a shopping and business centre linked by footbridge to the riverside Koskikeskus district.
locations.facilities: Former needle factory and spinning mill, now used as a commercial and business centre between Laukontori marketplace and Koskikeskus shopping centre.
locations.logistics: 0.5 km from Tampere Central Square.

locations.name: Levi Ski Resort
locations.setting: Finland's largest ski resort on Levi fell in Kittila, with 43 marked slopes and 27 lifts amid birch and pine wilderness, used in winter for skiing and Northern Lights and in summer for fell hiking under the midnight sun.
locations.known_for: The Grand Tour: A Scandi Flick (2022)

locations.name: Mediapolis
locations.setting: Media campus at broadcaster Yle's Tohloppi site in Tampere, with fully equipped television studios and a 1,500 square metre factory hall stage available for hire.
locations.facilities: Two Yle broadcast studios of 432 m2 (24 x 18 m) and 342 m2 (19 x 18 m) with tungsten lighting, hoists and 360-degree curtains; a 1,200 m2 Factory Hall (26 x 54.5 m, 10 m clear height); smaller TAMK and United studios of 133 and 198 m2; wardrobe and makeup rooms, six sound studios and edit stations.
locations.suitability: Studios are booked through a named contact per facility; the campus also offers production services, catering, event spaces and office facilities.
locations.logistics: 32,000 m2 campus in the Tohloppi district of Tampere where 1,000 to 1,100 people work and study daily

locations.name: Melo Power Plant
locations.setting: A hydroelectric power plant in Nokia near Tampere offering both industrial interiors and surrounding nature for productions, listed by Film Tampere as a filming location.
locations.logistics: Located at Melontie 59, 37140 Nokia, about 20 km from Tampere's central square

locations.name: Nokia Museums (Hinttala)
locations.setting: A local history museum in the town of Nokia occupying a relocated worker's house, part of a small cluster of preserved 19th and 20th century industrial-era homes.

locations.name: Parking Garages by Finnpark
locations.setting: A network of multi storey car parks operated by Finnpark in and around central Tampere, listed by Film Tampere as available filming locations.
locations.logistics: Filming enquiries for the parking garages are directed to Finnpark's Marketing Chief (contact published on the Film Tampere location page).

locations.name: Pekilo Performance and Event Venue
locations.setting: A former animal-feed factory building beside the closed Mantta pulp mill, converted into an exhibition and event space with variable rooms and a ceiling rising to 12 metres.

locations.name: Pirkkala Old Church
locations.setting: A wooden church built in 1921 in Pirkkala, with an adjoining cemetery, a church boat and a bird observation tower on the grounds.

locations.name: Pispala Area
locations.setting: A protected hillside neighbourhood in Tampere of narrow streets and restored wooden houses between two lakes, home to Rajaportti, the oldest public sauna in Finland.

locations.name: Pitkäniemi Hospital Area
locations.setting: Former psychiatric hospital on a lakeshore park in Nokia near Tampere, with stone buildings from the 1890s including an Italianate villa, in clinical use from 1900 until closure in 2024 and now largely vacant.
locations.facilities: Historical stone hospital buildings completed in 1894-1895 in parkland on the shore of Lake Pyhäjärvi, part of Tampere University Hospital. The former chief's residence ('the Castle') has Italian Renaissance-style columned terraces and now houses the Pitkäniemi Hospital Museum.
locations.logistics: 12.5 km from Tampere Central Square.

locations.name: Sarkanniemi Amusement Park
locations.setting: A lakeside amusement park in central Tampere combining rides, an aquarium, a planetarium, a children's zoo and the Nasinneula observation tower.

locations.name: Senate Square
locations.setting: Neoclassical square by Carl Ludvig Engel framed by Helsinki Cathedral, the Government Palace and the university, long used as a stand-in for imperial St Petersburg and Soviet-era Moscow.

locations.name: Sibelius Hall
locations.setting: A wooden concert hall on the shore of Lake Vesijarvi in Lahti, with a main hall, several conference rooms and a live music club, offering full event production and streaming services.
locations.facilities: Main hall (Paasali), Metsahalli, Puusepan Sali, conference rooms, restaurants and the Finlandia-klubi live music venue
locations.logistics: Located at Ankkurikatu 7, Lahti

locations.name: Stable Yards (Tallipiha)
locations.setting: A 19th century stable courtyard from the Finlayson factory community in Tampere, restored with Russian style cottages that now house craft shops and a cafe, listed by Film Tampere as a filming location.
locations.logistics: Located at Kuninkaankatu 4, about 0.7 km from Tampere's central square

locations.name: Suomenlinna
locations.setting: Sea fortress built from 1748 across a cluster of islands off Helsinki, with stone bastions, tunnels, dry docks and cobbled courtyards, now a UNESCO World Heritage site with museums and open parkland.
locations.logistics: Official site publishes separate instructions for filming and photography and a dedicated contact for bookings.

locations.name: Suvilahti
locations.setting: Former power plant and gasworks complex in Helsinki with red-brick industrial halls and open concrete yards, now a cultural venue mixing galleries, restaurants and a brewery inside the original industrial shells.
locations.facilities: Site explicitly offers outdoor and indoor space rental for events, festivals and photo shoots.
locations.logistics: Managed by Kiinteistö Oy Kaapelitalo; multiple independent tenants occupy separate buildings on the site.

locations.name: Tampere City Hall
locations.setting: A neo renaissance city hall from 1890 on Tampere's central square, with several period halls, listed by Film Tampere as a filming location.
locations.logistics: Located at Keskustori 10, at the edge of Tampere's central square

locations.name: Tampere Hall
locations.setting: Largest congress centre in the Nordic countries, a modern building beside Sorsapuisto park in central Tampere with a 1,756-seat main auditorium and several smaller halls used for concerts and conferences.

locations.name: Tampere Market Hall (Kauppahalli)
locations.setting: Largest market hall in the Nordic countries when it opened in 1901, a protected two-story brick building in central Tampere with roughly 30 food stalls, cafes and restaurants.
locations.facilities: 174 retail outlets, opened 1901; about 40 percent of outlets are cafes and restaurants (Film Tampere).
locations.logistics: Address Hameenkatu 19, 33200 Tampere; 0 km from the Central Square (Film Tampere).

locations.name: Tullikamari
locations.setting: A former customs warehouse in Tampere converted into a cultural venue with a large main hall and a smaller club space, used for concerts, theatre and festivals, listed by Film Tampere as a filming location.
locations.logistics: Located at Tullikamarin aukio 2, about 1 km from Tampere's central square

locations.name: Turku Castle
locations.setting: Medieval keep begun around 1280 at the mouth of the Aura river, expanded into a Renaissance bailey under Gustav Vasa in the 16th century, now a city museum with period rooms, banqueting halls and rentable event spaces.
locations.known_for: Sadan miekan mies (1951), The Girl King (2015)
locations.facilities: Rooms published for hire: Kuninkaan sali (King's Hall, up to 250), Linnan kirkko (Castle Church, up to 240), Kuningattaren sali (Queen's Hall, up to 180), Bryggman-sali (up to 120 for lectures, 80 for banquets), Eteläinen sali (Southern Hall, up to 100), Kuningattaren kamari (Queen's Chamber, up to 50), Herrainkellari (Gentlemen's Cellar, up to 30), plus courtyard areas.

photo.author: Markus Koljonen (Dilaudid) with thanks to Jontts and Turku Cathedral

locations.name: Vehoniemi Car Museum
locations.setting: A car museum on the Vehoniemi ridge near Kangasala, open since 1983, with a rotating display of vintage vehicles kept in running order.

locations.name: Viitaniemi Quarry
locations.setting: An open-pit feldspar quarry near Orivesi, worked from 1935 to 1965 for lithium-bearing feldspar, with gemstones still found among its waste rock piles.

locations.name: Abbaye de Saint-Michel-en-Thierache
locations.setting: A Benedictine abbey founded in 945 in Saint-Michel-en-Thierache, rebuilt several times, with a 17th century baroque facade, a central cloister, an abbey church, a chapter house and a refectory.

locations.name: Abbaye Royale de Fontevraud
locations.setting: Former royal abbey near Chinon founded in 1101, with a Romanesque church, medieval kitchens and cloisters plus an on-site hotel, its own site publishing information for film and TV shoots.
locations.suitability: The abbey has hosted film, documentary and music video shoots since the 1940s; interior and exterior spaces (cloisters, churches, gardens) are described as suited to crews of any size (own site).
locations.logistics: Truck access to on-site parking, dressing rooms, on-site accommodation and catering, and electrical connections (own site).

locations.name: Accor Arena
locations.setting: Multi-purpose indoor arena in Bercy seating up to about 20,300, built into a grass-covered pyramid, used for concerts, sport and large events.

locations.name: Aeroport Paris-Charles de Gaulle
locations.setting: France's main international airport north of Paris, with terminals, control-tower views and airside areas that operator Groupe ADP makes available for filming through a dedicated production service.

locations.name: Allianz Riviera
locations.setting: Nice football stadium with a translucent wave-shaped roof, home to OGC Nice and used for concerts and other large events.

locations.name: Aquaboulevard
locations.setting: Indoor and outdoor water park in the 15th arrondissement, with wave pools, slides and tropical-style planting, hired through its own professional booking service for shoots and events.

locations.name: Arenes de Nimes
locations.setting: Roman amphitheatre built around 100 AD in the centre of Nimes, seating up to 24,000 for its own ferias and concerts, with a covered arena floor usable for filming outside the events calendar.

locations.name: Base sous-marine de Saint-Nazaire (La Base)
locations.setting: Reinforced-concrete U-boat pens built by the German navy in WWII on the Saint-Nazaire docks, now holding exhibition halls, a climbing wall and a rooftop garden.

locations.name: Bassins de Lumières
locations.setting: Former WWII submarine pens on the Bordeaux docks converted into a digital art centre, with four raw concrete basins used for large-scale wall and floor projections.
locations.facilities: Two indoor spaces: the Citerne (155 sqm, 360-degree projection) and the Cube (220 sqm, soundproofed), plus elevated walkways and tiered seating. Overall capacity ranges from 50 to 900 for a cocktail reception or 50 to 700 for a seated dinner.
locations.suitability: The venue lists professional events as one of five event categories it hosts, alongside cocktails, seated dinners, and private visits.

locations.name: Bibliothèque nationale de France, site Richelieu
locations.setting: Historic national library building in central Paris with a 19th-century domed reading room and ornate galleries, reopened after a long restoration.
locations.facilities: At the Richelieu site, the Salle Ovale seats up to 220 for a dinner or holds up to 300 for a cocktail reception. Other hireable spaces are the Hall Vivienne, the Vivienne garden, and the Salon d'Honneur.
locations.suitability: Filming and photography require prior written authorization from BnF, covering the Richelieu, François-Mitterrand, Arsenal, Opéra and CTBnF sites; an exception applies only to images made for strictly private, non-commercial use.
locations.logistics: Richelieu site spaces can be hired from 6pm Wednesday to Sunday, and all day on Monday when the site is closed to the public.

locations.name: Bourse de Commerce, Pinault Collection
locations.setting: Former 19th-century grain exchange with a circular rotunda and glass dome, renovated by Tadao Ando with an internal concrete cylinder as a contemporary art museum.
locations.facilities: Ground-floor Salon and Passage (up to 800 for a cocktail reception or 220 for a seated dinner), Foyer on floor -1 (up to 300 for a cocktail reception), a semi-circular Auditorium (284 seats), the Petit Salon (up to 70 people), and the restaurant La Halle aux Grains (125 for a cocktail reception or 100 for a dinner).
locations.logistics: Private events run Monday to Thursday from 8:30-10:30am and from 7:30pm, and from 7pm on Tuesdays when the museum is closed to the public.

locations.name: Cap Sciences
locations.setting: Science centre inside Hangar 20, a former dockside cargo warehouse on the Garonne in Bordeaux, keeping the hangar's steel roof trusses over its exhibition floor, with halls listed to hire.
locations.facilities: 6 work spaces plus a terrace; kitchen equipment includes a service lift, large-capacity refrigerator, oven and washroom (own site).

locations.name: Centre Historique Minier (Lewarde Mining Centre)
locations.setting: Preserved coal mine museum in the former Delloye colliery, with pithead buildings, a headframe, underground galleries and workshops from the Nord-Pas-de-Calais coalfield.
locations.price_note: Meeting room hire from EUR 145 per half day (34-36 sqm rooms) up to EUR 1,000 per full day for the Auditorium Georges Delerue; technical support is a mandatory extra at EUR 35 per hour (own site, 2026 rates)
locations.facilities: Salle Jules Mousseron (70 sqm), Salle Lucien Jonas (36 sqm) and Salle Albert Bouquillon (34 sqm) meeting rooms, plus the Auditorium Georges Delerue (200 seats: 175 armchairs with a writing tablet, 22 folding seats and 3 wheelchair spaces, with a 45 sqm stage, a 4x3m screen and an audio system). Wheelchair accessible by lift.

locations.name: Chamonix-Mont-Blanc
locations.setting: Alpine resort town below Mont Blanc with cable cars up to the Aiguille du Midi and nearby glaciers, a base for mountaineering and skiing since the 19th century.

locations.name: Chartreuse de Neuville
locations.setting: A former Carthusian monastery near Montreuil-sur-Mer, restored around cloistered gardens, run by an association that rents out its halls for events alongside its heritage and cultural programme.

locations.name: Château d'If
locations.setting: 16th-century island fortress off Marseille used as a state prison into the 19th century, the setting of The Count of Monte Cristo and a location in The French Connection.
locations.facilities: 1,547 sqm of castle interior with several small rooms, 600 sqm of terraces, and a 1,700 sqm parade ground. The castle interior and terraces each hold up to 100 people standing; the parade ground holds up to 500 standing.
locations.suitability: Both interior and exterior filming are offered year-round, for films, series, documentaries and advertisements.

locations.name: Chateau l'Hospitalet
locations.setting: Wine estate on the La Clape massif near Narbonne, with vineyards, cellars, a hotel and restaurants around a courtyard, hosting its own annual jazz festival and grounds used for private events.

locations.name: Chateau La Coste
locations.setting: Organic vineyard estate near Aix-en-Provence with a sculpture trail and pavilions by architects including Tadao Ando and Renzo Piano, a hotel and restaurant, and grounds hired for weddings.

locations.name: Chemin de Fer de la Baie de Somme
locations.setting: Heritage steam and diesel railway running along the Somme bay between Le Crotoy, Saint-Valery-sur-Somme and Cayeux, with period stations and rolling stock.
locations.price_note: Private train charter from EUR 2,200 including tax for the Belle Époque steam train (March to September) or EUR 2,500 including tax for the 4 Saisons diesel train (October to February), plus meals at EUR 43 per adult and EUR 20 per child under 12 (own site, 2026 rates)
locations.facilities: Two heritage trains available for private charter: Belle Époque (steam, seats up to 115) and 4 Saisons (diesel, seats up to 96). Neither train is wheelchair accessible or pet-friendly.
locations.logistics: Lunch charter departs Saint-Valery at 12:00 with a meal stop on the sea wall from 12:10 to 14:15, returning at 15:20. Dinner charter departs the Saint-Valery Canal depot at 19:00, returning around 23:00-23:20. Booking requires a signed quote and a EUR 1,000 deposit, with the balance due 15 days before by bank cheque; no refund for late arrival or no-show.

locations.name: Cite de l'Automobile
locations.setting: Mulhouse car museum built around the Schlumpf brothers' collection, with several hundred vehicles under one roof lit by rows of replica cast-iron lamp posts, its site publishing venue-hire terms.
locations.facilities: Multiple hire spaces published: Espace Chefs-d'oeuvre 3,500 sqm; Salon Monaco 370 sqm (screen, speakers, wifi, video projector); Espace Course automobile 1,500 sqm; L'Espace Aventure automobile 9,500 sqm; L'Autodrome 270 sqm plus parking for up to 30 vehicles; Le Garage 425 sqm (own site).

locations.name: Cite de l'Espace
locations.setting: Space-themed science centre on the eastern edge of Toulouse, with a full-size Ariane rocket outdoors, planetarium domes and simulator halls, hired out for seminars and corporate events.

locations.name: Cite de la Mer
locations.setting: Maritime museum inside Cherbourg's 1933 Art Deco former transatlantic liner terminal, keeping the original departure hall, with a decommissioned submarine on display and dockside harbour views.
locations.suitability: The venue's events page lists tournage (filming) among the event types it hosts, alongside congress, seminar, exhibition, dinner, cocktail, show, private visit and ceremony (own site).

locations.name: Cité de la Mode et du Design
locations.setting: Former riverside customs warehouse on the Seine reclad in a green glass and steel skin, housing a design school, offices, a club and event floors over the water.

locations.name: Cité de la Voile Éric Tabarly (Keroman submarine base)
locations.setting: WWII U-boat pens on the Keroman peninsula in Lorient with roofs up to 7.5 metres thick, now holding a sailing museum, boatyards and a marina business park.
locations.facilities: Named spaces include the Auditorium, Karré Affaires (modular cocktail/reception space), two equipped meeting rooms, a permanent exhibition space, and Hall Pen Duick (modular for conferences, cocktails and exhibitions). Overall capacity ranges from 20 to 380 people. Equipped with tables, chairs, flipcharts, video projectors, UHD screens, sound systems, microphones and wifi.
locations.logistics: In Lorient, Brittany; about 3 hours from Paris by train, with Lorient station 10 minutes away. Pricing is by quotation only.

locations.name: Cité des Sciences et de l'Industrie
locations.setting: Large science museum in the Parc de la Villette built inside a converted 1960s abattoir hall, with the geodesic dome cinema La Géode standing alongside it.
locations.suitability: The site's commercial filming page groups available locations into interior exhibitions (Planetarium, Aquarium, Argonaute submarine), architecture (including the congress centre), behind-the-scenes areas (car parks, escalators, corridors, lifts) and exterior areas (moat, park), described as available by day and night. Past clients cited include TPS, Canal+, Yves Rocher and France Telecom (own site).

locations.name: Cité du Cinéma (Studios de Paris)
locations.setting: Studio campus in a converted riverside power station with sound stages, workshops and offices around a monumental glass-roofed nave.
locations.known_for: Lucy, Valerian and the City of a Thousand Planets
locations.facilities: Nine sound stages from 6,506 to 22,271 sq ft (largest Stage 5, 201 x 111 ft, about 2,070 m2) with 47 to 52.5 ft to the grid; offices, artist green rooms with hair and makeup, VIP green rooms, workshops and storage.
locations.suitability: Stages offered with adjoining offices, green rooms, workshops and storage inside the Cite du Cinema campus; the site keeps a list of productions shot there.
locations.logistics: 20 rue Ampere, Saint-Denis: 30 minutes from Charles de Gaulle airport, 20 minutes from Le Bourget, 30 to 40 minutes from central Paris; served by RER D and metro lines 13 and 14 (direct to Orly), A86 and A1 motorway access, two four-star hotels a five-minute walk away.

locations.name: Cite du Livre
locations.setting: Former match factory in Aix-en-Provence, converted into a library and performance complex that keeps its industrial brick shell and a large auditorium used by the Festival d'Aix.

locations.name: Cite du Train
locations.setting: One of the world's largest railway museums, in Mulhouse, with locomotives and carriages under a long-span roof and a reconstructed period station platform, published as available for hire and filming.
locations.facilities: Two covered halls of 6,000 sqm and 13,000 sqm plus 16,000 sqm of outdoor space; named filming locations include station platforms, a turntable and a signal box (own site).
locations.suitability: Site publishes a filming/shooting page offering a technical site survey, a custom quote, on-site assistance during filming, and support with procedures via the Mulhouse Alsace Agglomeration film office. Past productions cited include Arte, France Televisions and SWR/ARD (own site).

locations.name: Cité Frugès
locations.setting: Estate of concrete houses built by Le Corbusier and Pierre Jeanneret in Pessac in 1926 in flat-roofed cubic and terraced forms, UNESCO-listed since 2016.

locations.name: Cité Internationale Universitaire de Paris
locations.setting: Campus of more than 40 national residence halls in varied architectural styles on the southern edge of Paris, housing international students since the 1920s.
locations.facilities: 34-hectare campus with 47 architecturally varied buildings dating from 1925 onward, offered for professional events as well as filming; parking for trucks and production equipment is positioned close to the sets, with a dedicated on-site team supporting productions.
locations.suitability: Described by CIUP as France's first multi-set filming location, with both interior settings (art deco lounges, halls, corridors, staircases, offices) and exterior settings (building facades, landscaped grounds). States that no prefectural authorization is required to film there; more than 500 productions have shot there in 10 years.

locations.name: Cité Radieuse, Marseille
locations.setting: Le Corbusier's 1952 concrete apartment block on stilts in Marseille, with 337 duplex units, an internal shopping street and a rooftop terrace.

locations.name: Couvent du Pouy
locations.setting: A 19th century convent on the edge of Dax, empty for over a decade, with a chapel, cloister galleries around a courtyard garden, and rooms and offices on three floors, listed by the regional film commission.

locations.name: Écomusée Creusot Montceau
locations.setting: Industrial heritage network around the former Schneider steelworks in Le Creusot, with the Château de la Verrerie glassworks-turned-mansion as its main site.

locations.name: Entrepot Beraud-Sudreau
locations.setting: A 10,000 square metre former warehouse in Brive-la-Gaillarde, split into two halls of 6,000 and 4,000 square metres with 200 square metres of offices, listed by the regional film commission.
locations.facilities: Two buildings of 6,000 and 4,000 square metres including 200 square metres of offices

locations.name: Escat
locations.setting: A former tobacco-processing plant in Bergerac with five buildings totalling 42,000 square metres, offered by the regional film commission for productions needing large industrial floor space.
locations.facilities: Five buildings of 20,000, 5,500, 5,500, 5,500 and 5,500 square metres

locations.name: Étretat Cliffs
locations.setting: White chalk cliffs with natural arches and a freestanding needle rising above a pebble beach on the Alabaster Coast.

locations.name: Familistere de Guise
locations.setting: A 19th century workers' housing complex in Guise built by industrialist Jean-Baptiste Godin, with glazed courtyards and communal apartment wings, now a museum that also hosts corporate events.

locations.name: France-Tabac
locations.setting: A former tobacco warehouse complex on the edge of Sarlat-la-Caneda, five buildings totalling 14,400 square metres, listed by the Perigord film office for set construction and large interiors.
locations.facilities: Five buildings of 6,235, 2,700, 2,160, 2,160 and 1,141 square metres

locations.name: Futuroscope
locations.setting: Multimedia theme park north of Poitiers built around futuristic pavilions and a lake, with cinema domes and landscaped outdoor sets, offering seminar and private event hire outside opening hours.

locations.name: Gare Saint Sauveur
locations.setting: Former goods yard of a 19th-century Lille railway station, now an exhibition and events venue keeping the open shed structure and platform-level halls of the original depot.

locations.name: Grand Port Maritime de Marseille
locations.setting: France's largest port, with the working container terminals and warehouses of Marseille-Fos and the historic Joliette basin, with its own published filming-permit process for productions.
locations.suitability: Filming within the port (Marseille or Fos-sur-Mer basins) requires an authorization convention; drone footage needs a separate authorization from the Harbormaster; filming at facilities occupied by port-based companies needs that company's written permission (own site).
locations.logistics: Applications should allow about 3 weeks after the file is processed; required documents include a KBIS (less than 3 months old), bank details, authorised signatory details, an on-site contact name, an insurance certificate covering the filming dates and a VAT number (own site).

locations.name: Halle Tony Garnier
locations.setting: A vast steel-framed former livestock market hall of 1864 in central Lyon, converted into the city's largest standing-capacity venue for concerts, trade fairs and exhibitions.

locations.name: Haras National de Lamballe
locations.setting: State stud farm founded in 1825 in a former army barracks in Lamballe, with stone stable blocks around a courtyard and a riding arena, its own site listing hire for weddings and seminars.

locations.name: Haras National du Pin
locations.setting: France's oldest national stud, an 18th-century complex of stables around a formal chateau-style courtyard in the Orne countryside, with an equestrian arena and grounds listed for seminar hire.

locations.name: Hôpital Bicêtre
locations.setting: Large hospital complex south of Paris with historic pavilions and a tall water reservoir building, listed by AP-HP among the sites it regularly opens to film crews.
locations.suitability: All filming at AP-HP hospitals is subject to prior authorization; arrangements must respect the image rights of patients, staff and visitors as well as hospital regulations. Filming gives rise to a fee for occupying public domain space, based on an internal AP-HP tariff scale that is not published online.

locations.name: Hôpital Maritime de Berck
locations.setting: Seafront AP-HP hospital in Berck-sur-Mer built as a 19th-century marine sanatorium, named on the AP-HP's list of hospitals that regularly welcome film shoots.
locations.suitability: All filming at AP-HP hospitals is subject to prior authorization; arrangements must respect the image rights of patients, staff and visitors as well as hospital regulations. Filming gives rise to a fee for occupying public domain space, based on an internal AP-HP tariff scale that is not published online.

locations.name: Hôpital Raymond-Poincaré
locations.setting: Rehabilitation hospital in Garches with early 20th-century pavilion wards and gardens, one of the AP-HP sites named as regularly opened for commercial filming.
locations.suitability: All filming at AP-HP hospitals is subject to prior authorization; arrangements must respect the image rights of patients, staff and visitors as well as hospital regulations. Filming gives rise to a fee for occupying public domain space, based on an internal AP-HP tariff scale that is not published online.

locations.name: Hopital Saint-Cyr
locations.setting: A 19th century hospital in central Villeneuve-sur-Lot, in use until 2015, with a neoclassical arcaded facade, a painted chapel, a former apothecary and wards over three floors around a wooded park.
locations.facilities: Large lorry-accessible car park, water and electricity available on site

locations.name: Hôpital Saint-Louis
locations.setting: Working Paris hospital built around an early 17th-century brick and stone quadrilateral courtyard, one of the AP-HP sites named as regularly hosting commercial filming.
locations.suitability: All filming at AP-HP hospitals is subject to prior authorization; arrangements must respect the image rights of patients, staff and visitors as well as hospital regulations. Filming gives rise to a fee for occupying public domain space, based on an internal AP-HP tariff scale that is not published online.

locations.name: Institut Lumière
locations.setting: Museum in the former Lumière family home in Lyon, dedicated to Auguste and Louis Lumière and the birth of cinema, close to the site of their original factory.
locations.facilities: Hangar du Premier-Film: 300 sqm, seats 220 for a dinner or 300 for a cocktail reception, plus an adjoining cinema seating 269 (with 8 wheelchair spaces), 3 plasma screens, 2 x 35mm projectors and 1 digital projector. Jardin d'Hiver at Villa Lumière: 60 sqm, 35 seated or 70 for a cocktail reception. Villa Lumière also has two screening rooms in the basement.
locations.logistics: 25 rue du Premier-Film, Lyon 8e; 6 minutes from Bellecour, 15 minutes from Part-Dieu station, and next to the Monplaisir-Lumière stop on metro line D. Free public parking with 54 spaces beside the Hangar.

locations.name: La Cite du Vin
locations.setting: Twisting glass and aluminium tower on Bordeaux's Garonne quays, built around a wine museum and a top-floor tasting room, with function spaces used for private events and film screenings.

locations.name: La Condition Publique
locations.setting: Former municipal wool-conditioning warehouse in Roubaix, a long glass-roofed 19th-century industrial hall now run as a cultural and event venue.
locations.facilities: More than 10,000 sqm across named spaces: Rue couverte, Verrière, Halle A, B and C, Plateau Coucke et Labos, Le Club, L'Alim, and Les Toits Terrasses. Overall capacity ranges from 10 to 5,000 people.
locations.suitability: Filming ("tournages") is listed among the event types the venue hosts, alongside meetings, conferences, evening events, corporate seminars, fashion shows and team-building.

locations.name: La Défense
locations.setting: Purpose-built business district west of Paris with high-rise office towers, an elevated pedestrian esplanade and the Grande Arche at its western end.

locations.name: La Friche la Belle de Mai
locations.setting: Former SEITA tobacco factory in Marseille converted into a multi-storey arts complex, with raw concrete floors, a rooftop garden and a skatepark, hired out through its own privatisation service.
locations.facilities: Accommodates 10 to 4,000 people; La Cartonnerie is a 2,500 sqm modular space; the roof terrace is 8,000 sqm with views over Marseille; meeting rooms hold 10 to 150 people; Place des Horizons is a modular covered plaza (own site).

locations.name: La Piscine, Musee d'Art et d'Industrie Andre Diligent
locations.setting: 1932 Art Deco municipal swimming pool in Roubaix converted into a museum, keeping its tiled pool basin, stained glass and rows of former changing cubicles as exhibition space.

locations.name: La Sucriere
locations.setting: Former sugar warehouse on the Confluence docks in Lyon, a long brick and concrete shed on the Saone quayside, now an exhibition and events venue run by a professional events operator.
locations.facilities: 5,100 sqm covered in total, including 3,800 sqm of event space and 1,700 sqm of exhibition space; 5 balcony terraces overlooking the Saone; capacity up to 1,500 seated, 4,000 for a cocktail reception or 1,000 for a conference; riverside privatisation is also possible (own site).
locations.logistics: Accessible by tram T1/T2 to Hotel de Region Montrochet and by bus S1; parking available at the nearby Confluence shopping centre and surrounding paid spaces (own site).

locations.name: Lagora
locations.setting: A disused 10,000 square metre leisure and commercial complex in Angouleme, split across three buildings and listed by the regional film commission for large-scale sets.
locations.facilities: Three buildings of 3,650, 2,411 and 1,552 square metres

locations.name: Le 104 (Centquatre-Paris)
locations.setting: Former municipal funeral parlour in northern Paris with two vast glass-roofed halls, now an arts centre with studios and space hired for events and shoots.
locations.facilities: Nef Curial: 1,026 sqm plus 1,000 sqm of circulation space, seats 1,000 or holds 1,780 standing. Jardin: 420 sqm, 250 seated or 600 standing. Salle 400: 400 sqm, 395 seated or 740 standing. Salle 200: 300 sqm, 190 seated or 580 standing. Écuries: 2,000 sqm across one main hall and 8 sections, 180-800 seated depending on configuration or 1,500+ standing. Also two meeting rooms (20-40 seated), a workshop space (70 seated/95 standing) and a catering area (80 seated/150 standing). Loading dock and on-site parking available.
locations.suitability: Described as suitable for fashion shows, cocktails, trade fairs, dinners, sports events, conferences, seminars and performances.

locations.name: Le Bateau Feu
locations.setting: A 20th century national theatre in central Dunkirk with a large main stage and backstage artist workshops, named by the regional film commission among its exceptional filming locations.

locations.name: Le Fresnoy
locations.setting: A national contemporary art school in Tourcoing built inside a former early 20th century entertainment complex, with production studios under a large suspended roof and rentable spaces for private events.
locations.facilities: Production studios, a cinema, a restaurant, rooftop access, rooms available for private hire

locations.name: Le Grand Hôtel Cabourg
locations.setting: Belle Époque seafront hotel in Cabourg that inspired Marcel Proust's Grand Hôtel de Balbec, with period public rooms overlooking the beach.

locations.name: Le Grand Rex
locations.setting: 1932 Art Deco single-screen cinema and concert hall on Boulevard Poissonniere, with a domed starlit auditorium seating over 2,700, hired out for premieres, shows and filming.
locations.facilities: Grande Salle seats 800 to 2,700; other spaces include Les Halls (800), Le Club (350), Rex Infinite (285), Rex 3 (238), Rex 5 (163), Rex 4 (122), Rex 7 (109) and Rex 6 (78); technical equipment includes projection, sound, microphones and internet access (own site).
locations.logistics: Address 1 Boulevard Poissonniere, 75002 Paris; nearest metro Bonne Nouvelle (own site).

locations.name: Le Silo
locations.setting: 1920s grain silo on Marseille's Arenc docks, gutted and rebuilt inside as a concert and conference hall while keeping its raw concrete exterior, hired for shows and corporate events.

locations.name: Le Train Bleu
locations.setting: Belle Époque restaurant inside Gare de Lyon station, listed as a historic monument since 1972, with gilded ceilings and large painted murals of French regions.
locations.known_for: La Femme Nikita (1990), Mr. Bean's Holiday (2007), Micmacs (2009), Place Vendôme (1998)

locations.name: Le Tripostal
locations.setting: Former postal sorting depot beside Lille-Flandres station, converted into a bare-shell exhibition hall with high ceilings and loading-bay access, hired for shows and events.

locations.name: Les Abattoirs, Musee - Frac Occitanie Toulouse
locations.setting: Former municipal slaughterhouse on the Garonne in Toulouse, converted into a contemporary art museum that keeps the original brick halls, steel roof trusses and a loading yard.
locations.price_note: Room hire published per space: Salle du Conseil EUR 1,000 (20 people); Auditorium EUR 3,000 (up to 199 seated); Hall d'Accueil EUR 3,000 (150 people, 180 sqm); Salle Picasso EUR 8,000 (150 people); La Nef EUR 8,000 to 32,000 depending on headcount; outdoor spaces (up to 2,000 people) on custom quote (own site).
locations.facilities: La Nef is 38 m long and 10 m wide with brick walls and high ceilings; Salle Picasso is 15 m by 12 m; the Auditorium stage is 10.8 m long and 3.8 m deep with 4 m under the ceiling; Hall d'Accueil is 180 sqm (own site).
locations.logistics: Security staffing is mandatory outside operating hours, at extra cost; all interior spaces are accessible to mobility-impaired visitors; no catering exclusivity and no corkage fee (own site).

locations.name: Les Deux Magots
locations.setting: Historic Saint-Germain-des-Prés cafe with a covered terrace and wood-panelled interior, a literary and artist meeting place since the late 19th century.

photo.author: Cheng-en Cheng from Taichung City, Taiwan

locations.name: Les Docks, Marseille
locations.setting: Row of 19th-century dockside warehouses on the Joliette waterfront, restored around an internal courtyard of offices, shops and restaurants.

locations.name: Les Fermes de Marie
locations.setting: Alpine hotel in Megève built from reassembled 18th and 19th-century farm buildings, with a spa and chalet-style interiors furnished in reclaimed wood.

locations.name: Les Frigos
locations.setting: Former refrigerated railway goods depot near the old Paris-Ivry station, now artist studios behind a graffiti-covered brick facade, with raw interiors and a covered yard in the 13th arrondissement.

locations.name: Les Halles de Lyon Paul Bocuse
locations.setting: Covered food market in Lyon with about fifty stalls of butchers, cheesemongers, bakers and small restaurants, named after chef Paul Bocuse.
locations.facilities: 8,000 sqm total, with two indoor terraces and one outdoor terrace. La Verrière (mezzanine) holds 50 to 300 for cocktails or seated dining; L'Espace Convivial (partial closure) holds 500 to 1,000; La Balade Gourmande (full privatisation of the market) holds 1,000 to 3,500. Wheelchair accessible, with nearby parking and EV charging.

locations.name: Les Studios de Saint-Menet
locations.setting: A former chocolate factory in Marseille's Saint-Menet district converted into roughly 30,000 square metres of sound stages, office space and three usable rooftop terraces across three buildings.
locations.facilities: Private parking for over 200 vehicles, ready-to-shoot sets, three practicable roof terraces, a green-screen studio
locations.suitability: Sound stages and office space for film and TV production

locations.name: Les Subsistances
locations.setting: Former military supply depot on the Saone quays in Lyon, now a centre for performing-arts creation with rehearsal halls, a courtyard and studios, published as available to hire.
locations.facilities: La Verriere and La Boulangerie each take up to 2,000 people for a cocktail reception or 800 for a seated dinner (La Verriere available April to October only; the two can be combined); Le Hangar has 610 sqm total with a 300 sqm stage and fixed seating for 220 (up to 400 with extra chairs); La Terrasse holds 20 to 200 people; Les Plateaux is 130 sqm, seating 126 for a conference/show or about 20 for workshops; L'Accueil holds 30 for meetings or 50 for a cocktail (own site).

locations.name: Lycee Gaston Monnerville
locations.setting: A working vocational and general secondary school in Cahors, listed by the local film office as an available shooting location for productions needing classrooms and school corridors.

locations.name: Marche International de Rungis
locations.setting: The world's largest wholesale food market, south of Paris, with vast refrigerated halls, loading docks and pre-dawn trading floors, offering event space and press filming through its own services team.
locations.suitability: Every filming request must go through a formal authorization process with the SEMMARIS communications department (own site).
locations.logistics: Requests must be submitted at least 3 days in advance, described as non-negotiable because market operators work staggered schedules; applicants must specify subject, format, needs, synopsis, broadcast date and equipment used (own site).

locations.name: MuCEM
locations.setting: Marseille museum in a concrete cube wrapped in a black lattice screen, linked by a footbridge to the 13th-century Fort Saint-Jean at the harbour entrance.
locations.suitability: Accepts filming for documentaries, adverts, feature and short films, series, music videos and trailers, in Building J4 and Fort Saint-Jean (parade ground, courtyard, officers' gallery). Filming is possible on Tuesdays all day, other days by request; images of the J4 building are subject to copyright restrictions. MuCEM also hosts more than 100 corporate events a year, including filming, among seminars, conferences, team building and galas.

locations.name: Musee de l'Air et de l'Espace
locations.setting: Aerospace museum built around historic hangars at the edge of Paris-Le Bourget airport, with aircraft, open apron and runway views bookable through its own filming and photography service.
locations.suitability: Filming takes place only on Mondays, the museum's weekly closing day. Available spaces include the Boeing 747, the Concorde, WWII, Inter-War, Space and Helicopter halls, the control tower, the tarmac, the planetarium and terraces. Extra staffing, aircraft relocation, special technical work and copyright royalties are billed separately from the standard tariff (own site).

locations.name: Omaha Beach
locations.setting: Stretch of Normandy coast where American forces landed on D-Day, 6 June 1944, backed by bluffs, the American Cemetery and the Overlord Museum.

photo.author: Chief Photographer's Mate (CPHoM) Robert F. Sargent

locations.name: Palace of Versailles
locations.setting: Baroque royal palace with the Hall of Mirrors, state apartments, vast formal gardens and two smaller palaces in the park.
locations.suitability: The estate publishes a dedicated page for organising filming (tournage) on the Domaine de Versailles, alongside gala dinners, cocktails, concerts and private prestige visits; capacity and presentation of each space are said to be listed on a page per space (own site).

locations.name: Palais de Justice Historique de Lyon
locations.setting: 24-column neoclassical courthouse on the Saone in Vieux Lyon, its listed interior including a vast public hall, still used for hearings and available for filming by arrangement with the Cour d'appel.

locations.name: Palais des Festivals et des Congres
locations.setting: Cannes' seafront convention centre and home of the Cannes Film Festival, with cinema auditoriums, exhibition halls and the red-carpet staircase, hired for congresses and events year round.

locations.name: Palais Garnier
locations.setting: 19th-century opera house with a grand marble staircase, a gilded foyer and a ceiling painted by Chagall, home to the Paris Opera Ballet.
locations.facilities: Public areas hold up to 2,000 people for a cocktail reception; the Grand Foyer seats up to 700 for a gala dinner. Other hireable spaces include the Avant-Foyer, Rotonde des abonnés, Rotonde du glacier and Galerie Aline Foriel-Destezet.

locations.name: Parc naturel régional de Camargue
locations.setting: Rhône delta wetland reserve of lagoons, salt pans and marshland grazed by black bulls and white horses, managed as a regional nature park.

locations.name: Paris Expo Porte de Versailles
locations.setting: Paris's largest exhibition centre, eight halls totalling over 200,000 square metres beside the ring road, hired for trade shows, corporate events and filming through operator Viparis.

locations.name: Phare de Cordouan
locations.setting: Working lighthouse on a rock at the mouth of the Gironde estuary, built from 1584 with a royal apartment and chapel inside, UNESCO-listed since 2021.

locations.name: Piscine Molitor
locations.setting: Art Deco outdoor and indoor swimming pool complex from 1929 in western Paris, restored as part of a hotel with the original tiled pools kept in use.
locations.facilities: Salons Longchamp & Auteuil and Salon Murat each hold up to 130 (theatre style); Salon Murat is 135 sqm and doubles as an urban art gallery. Le Solarium rooftop is 160 sqm, holds up to 130, and is open May to September only. Restaurant Molitor is 200 sqm for up to 150. Bar Bikini is 75 sqm for up to 50. Configurations offered: theatre, cabaret, U-shape, classroom, cocktail. Indoor and outdoor pools on site.

locations.name: Pont Eiffel sur le Lot
locations.setting: A 19th century metal footbridge over the Lot river at Bouzies, on the riverside towpath through the gorge, listed as a filming location by the Lot department's film office.

locations.name: Provence Studios
locations.setting: A studio complex on 22 hectares near Martigues with sixteen sound stages up to 2,400 square metres, two 18,000 square metre backlots and ready-built prison, police station and courtroom sets.
locations.known_for: Titane, The Serpent Queen, Gaston Lagaffe
locations.facilities: 1,000 sqm of production offices, 8,000 sqm of workshops and joinery, dressing rooms, a virtual production LED stage of 14 by 14 metres
locations.suitability: Ready-built prison, police station, morgue, hospital room and courtroom sets, plus two exterior backlots

locations.name: Site Le Corbusier, Firminy
locations.setting: Le Corbusier's Firminy-Vert complex, completed after his death, with a raw-concrete Unite d'habitation apartment block, a stadium and a church, its visitor centre offering room hire for seminars.

locations.name: Stade de France
locations.setting: National stadium in Saint-Denis seating over 80,000, built for the 1998 World Cup and used for major sport, concerts and ceremonies.

locations.name: Station F
locations.setting: Former Halle Freyssinet railway freight depot, a single steel-framed hall over 300 metres long in southeast Paris, now a start-up campus with open floors and event space.

locations.name: Theatre Antique d'Orange
locations.setting: Best-preserved Roman theatre stage wall in Europe, in Orange, with tiered stone seating for around 9,000, used every summer as the main stage of the Choregies opera festival.

locations.name: Theatre Antique de Vienne
locations.setting: Roman theatre cut into a hillside above Vienne on the Rhone, with tiered stone seating for around 7,000, used every summer as the main stage of the Jazz a Vienne festival.

locations.name: Transpalux
locations.setting: A film lighting and grip company's premises in Saint-Yrieix-sur-Charente near Angoulême, offered by the regional film commission as three separate industrial halls of 487 to 710 square metres.
locations.facilities: Three buildings of 603.7, 710.4 and 487.1 square metres

locations.name: Tribunal de Paris
locations.setting: Renzo Piano's 160-metre glass courthouse tower at Porte de Clichy, housing Paris's civil and criminal courts around a public hall and stacked courtroom floors, with filming possible by arrangement.

locations.name: TSF Studios d'Aquitaine
locations.setting: A 400 square metre studio building run by a film equipment rental company in Bègles, in the Bordeaux metropolitan area, listed by the regional film commission for shoots needing a single controllable space.
locations.facilities: One building of 400 square metres

locations.name: Viaduc de Millau
locations.setting: Cable-stayed road bridge across the Tarn valley, the tallest of its kind in the world at 343 metres, carrying the A75 motorway.

locations.name: Villa Savoye
locations.setting: Le Corbusier's white 1931 villa in Poissy raised on thin pilotis, with ribbon windows, a roof garden and a spiral ramp, managed as a national monument.
locations.facilities: Interior capacity up to 70 people; garden/exterior capacity up to 450.
locations.suitability: Available for filming and photography year-round except during exhibitions. Images made at Villa Savoye are subject to image rights managed by the Fondation Le Corbusier and ADAGP.

locations.name: Vulcania
locations.setting: Volcano-themed science park built into the Auvergne hillside near Clermont-Ferrand, with underground galleries and a crater-shaped amphitheatre, listing seminar and private event hire.

locations.name: Alte Feuerwache Mannheim
locations.setting: A disused early-20th-century fire station converted into a cultural centre, keeping its engine hall, brick facade and yard, now hired for concerts and events.

locations.name: Alte Klinik Greifenstein
locations.setting: A former specialist lung clinic at Waldhof in Greifenstein, in operation until 2020, with about 4,500 square metres of floor space across an older building and later extensions.

locations.name: Alte Oper Frankfurt
locations.setting: Rebuilt 1880s opera house in Frankfurt, now a concert and congress venue with a restored historicist facade and a modern auditorium behind it.
locations.facilities: Grosser Saal (Grand Hall): 2,064 m2, 17.5 m high, up to 2,434 in row seating, 1,150 to 1,228 banquet, 644 parliamentary. Mozart Saal: 817 m2, 6.2 m high, up to 718 row seating, 362 to 376 banquet, 220 parliamentary. Salons (Schumann, Liszt, Mendelssohn, Telemann): 75 to 83 m2, 2.5 to 5.5 m high, 30 to 72 people depending on layout. Foyers (Paul Hindemith, Clara Schumann, Hertie, Albert Mangelsdorff): 260 to 880 m2, capacity 136 to 265.

locations.name: Alte Schokoladenfabrik Oderwitz
locations.setting: A fully vacant former chocolate factory site in Oderwitz near Goerlitz, with an administration building with a period staircase alongside disused production and storage halls.

locations.name: Autostadt Wolfsburg
locations.setting: Car-brand visitor park beside the Volkswagen plant in Wolfsburg, with pavilions, glass delivery towers, a museum hall and landscaped grounds beside a canal.

locations.name: Bauhaus Dessau
locations.setting: 1926 Bauhaus school building by Walter Gropius in Dessau, a UNESCO World Heritage site with glass curtain walls, workshop wings, studio flats and an auditorium.

locations.name: Bauhaus-Universitat Weimar
locations.setting: The founding site of the Bauhaus school, with Henry van de Velde's Art Nouveau studio building and later modernist extensions still used as a working university.

locations.name: Bavaria Filmstadt
locations.setting: Working film studio complex in Grünwald near Munich with sound stages, a backlot and standing sets used for German film and television production since the 1920s.

photo.author: Unbekannte Autoren und Grafiker; Scan von Auktionshaus Vladimir Gutowski

locations.name: Bayerisches Eisenbahnmuseum
locations.setting: A former steam locomotive depot at Nordlingen with a working roundhouse, turntable and yard of preserved steam and diesel engines.

locations.name: Beelitz-Heilstätten
locations.setting: Sprawling former tuberculosis sanatorium and military hospital south of Berlin with dozens of derelict Wilhelmine-era pavilions, overgrown grounds and a former alpine slide building.

locations.name: Berlin-Hohenschönhausen Memorial
locations.setting: Former Stasi remand prison in Lichtenberg with preserved interrogation rooms, cells and a prisoner transport van, run as a memorial site open for research and filming about East Germany.

locations.name: Boardinghaus Weinberg Campus
locations.setting: Three late classicist villas grouped around a courtyard at the edge of Halle's Weinberg Campus technology park, now listed guest houses with one and two room serviced apartments.

locations.name: Breuninger Kaufhaus Erfurt
locations.setting: A department store built in the 1990s in Erfurt's historic city centre, designed to fit the scale of the surrounding 1,250 year old old town while offering large modern retail floors inside.

locations.name: Container Terminal Halle (Saale)
locations.setting: A working inland freight terminal on the Saale river in Halle, with rail and road links, a harbour basin, quayside, tracks, weighing and loading equipment across a large industrial site.

locations.name: Deutsche Nationalbibliothek (Deutsche Buecherei)
locations.setting: The Leipzig home of Germany's national library, founded in 1912 and holding around 20 million items, in a purpose-built early 20th century building on Deutscher Platz.

locations.name: Deutsches Museum
locations.setting: Large science and technology museum on an island in the Isar in Munich, with historic machine halls, a planetarium and collections spanning mining to aerospace.

locations.name: Duisburg Innenhafen
locations.setting: A former inland harbour of grain silos and warehouses redeveloped into offices, restaurants and waterside promenades, keeping its industrial brick shells.

locations.name: Ehemaliges Kaufhaus Hermann Tietz Gera
locations.setting: A former department store in Gera dating to 1882, one of the first built by the Hermann Tietz chain, with the grand facade the company used to signal the scale of its business inside.

locations.name: Eisenbahnmuseum Bochum-Dahlhausen
locations.setting: A preserved steam-era railway depot with a roundhouse, turntable, workshops and sidings of historic locomotives and carriages.

locations.name: Elbphilharmonie
locations.setting: Concert hall on the Elbe in Hamburg's HafenCity, built above a former cocoa warehouse with a glass wave-shaped upper structure, a public plaza and two auditoriums.
locations.facilities: Grand Hall: standard capacity 2,091, reducible to about 1,555 in some configurations; stage about 260 m2, playable area about 18 x 15 m; 31 electrically operated height-adjustable platforms; organ; foyers with cloakrooms and bars on multiple floors. Recital Hall: 532 in standard configuration (14.5 x 6.3 m stage), 388 with a larger 14.5 x 11.8 m stage, 210 seated for banquets; base area 435 m2 (14.5 x 30 m) with seating removed; mobile auditorium and stage elements.
locations.logistics: Two loading zones with service lifts on the south side require advance arrangement; artists access via the Artists' Entrance on the south/port side. Visitor access to the concert area is only via the Elbphilharmonie Plaza, so every visitor needs a ticket.

locations.name: Ferropolis
locations.setting: Open-air museum on a peninsula in a former lignite mining lake near Gräfenhainichen, displaying five giant excavators and dredgers on a bare industrial ground used for festivals and events.
locations.facilities: Arena covers 14,000 m2 with a maximum of 25,000 visitors; seated configurations include 3,250 seated/6,500 standing, 4,820 standing steps, or up to 13,500 to 14,000 in the arena. Buildings include the Orangerie (560 m2), a mechanical workshop, an auxiliary workshop and admin areas (80 m2). On-site parking for 400 cars (7,000 more at the nearby federal highway), 10 bus spaces, 1,000 bike spaces and a heliport. Power supply: 782 kW for stage lighting and other uses, 248 kW for audio, with six distribution points around the arena. Water supply up to 13.32 m3/h, wastewater capacity 47.34 m3/h. Fixed sanitation for about 10,000 visitors, partly wheelchair accessible, plus a medical care room.

locations.name: Flughafen Berlin-Gatow
locations.setting: A former military airfield on the western edge of Berlin, now the Bundeswehr's air force museum, with a control tower, runway and hangars holding historic aircraft.

locations.name: Flughafen Dresden International
locations.setting: Dresden's airport, with a terminal built in 2001 in a glazed contemporary industrial style and Saxony's first underground S-Bahn station in its lower level.

locations.name: Flughafen Leipzig/Halle
locations.setting: An intercontinental airport between Leipzig and Halle, expanded around 2000 with a central terminal combining a railway station, multi storey car park and passenger check-in in one complex.

locations.name: Frankfurt Bankenviertel
locations.setting: Frankfurt's financial district of glass office towers grouped around the old town and the river Main, the only high-rise skyline of its kind in Germany.

locations.name: Frauenkirche Dresden
locations.setting: A baroque domed church rebuilt after wartime destruction, on Dresden's Neumarkt square, with a large sandstone dome and an ornate galleried interior.

locations.name: Funkhaus Berlin
locations.setting: A former East German state radio headquarters on the river Spree, with wood-panelled studios, offices and a large concert hall, run today as an event and production venue.

locations.name: Gasometer Oberhausen
locations.setting: 117-metre disused gas holder in Oberhausen converted into an exhibition hall, with a vast cylindrical interior used for large-scale installations.

locations.name: Gedenkstaette Hoheneck
locations.setting: A listed former prison complex in Stollberg with a main tract and three wings; cells occupied the south and west wings over four floors, and the north wing held workshop production lines.

locations.name: Georg-Gassmann-Stadion
locations.setting: Marburg's athletics stadium in the Ockershausen district, with a modern 400 metre synthetic running track and long jump, shot put and pole vault facilities.

locations.name: Glaeserne Manufaktur (Volkswagen)
locations.setting: Volkswagen's Transparent Factory in central Dresden, opened in 2001, where car assembly takes place behind glass walls visible to visitors alongside a showroom.

locations.name: Glasmanufaktur Harzkristall
locations.setting: One of Germany's few remaining working glassworks, at Derenburg in the Harz, where visitors can watch traditional glassblowing on the factory floor alongside a cafe and shop.

locations.name: Goethe-Universitaet Frankfurt am Main
locations.setting: One of Germany's largest universities, with more than 158 degree programmes spread across four campuses in Frankfurt, linked by the city's public transport network.

locations.name: Görlitz Old Town
locations.setting: War-spared old town of around 4,000 listed buildings ranging from Gothic and Renaissance to Baroque and Wilhelminian styles.
locations.known_for: The Grand Budapest Hotel, Inglourious Basterds, The Reader

locations.name: Grandhotel Schloss Bensberg
locations.setting: A former hunting palace above Cologne converted into a hotel, with baroque state rooms, a park and a modern spa wing.
locations.facilities: Ballsaal: meeting up to 180, banquet 240, reception 300. Eventhalle: meeting up to 250, reception 300. Bel Etage: reception up to 200. Salon Medici & Goethe: meeting/reception up to 100, banquet 80. Salon Alberti: meeting/reception up to 60. Salon Zanetti: meeting/reception up to 40. Gewoelbekeller (vaulted cellar): banquet up to 30, reception up to 50. Smaller boardrooms (Business Lounge, Library, Salon Habsburg) seat up to 12 to 20.

locations.name: Gymnasium St. Augustin zu Grimma
locations.setting: A grammar school in Grimma founded in 1450, housed since the 19th century in the former Augustinian monastery buildings, with its current facade dating from a full 1891 rebuild.

locations.name: Halle-Neustadt (noerdliche Neustadt)
locations.setting: A large prefabricated socialist new town built from 1964 to house workers near the Buna and Leuna chemical plants, originally planned with generous greenery and public art between the blocks.

locations.name: Hamburg Rathaus
locations.setting: Neo-Renaissance city hall of 1897 on the Rathausmarkt in Hamburg, with a 112-metre tower, an ornate facade and several hundred rooms including ceremonial halls.

locations.name: Hansaviertel Berlin
locations.setting: A postwar modernist housing estate built for the 1957 Interbau exhibition, with apartment towers and low-rise blocks by international architects set in parkland near the Tiergarten.

locations.name: Hauptbahnhof Frankfurt
locations.setting: Frankfurt's main station, Germany's second busiest long-distance rail hub, with a broad historicist concourse building where travellers from many routes cross paths.

locations.name: Hauptbahnhof Leipzig
locations.setting: Leipzig's main station, with a nearly 300 metre long concourse building and a six-vault steel platform hall, built with a strong symmetrical layout on both sides of the tracks.

locations.name: Hauptgebaeude FSU Jena
locations.setting: The main Art Nouveau building of Friedrich Schiller University Jena, opened in 1908 for the university's 350th anniversary, with an asymmetrical three to four storey facade.

locations.name: Heidelberg University
locations.setting: Germany's oldest university, with a baroque Old University building, a Great Hall and a historic student prison around Universitätsplatz in Heidelberg's old town.

locations.name: Hellerau
locations.setting: Early twentieth-century garden city on the edge of Dresden built around the Hellerau Festival Theatre, with modernist workshop housing and a rhythmic-gymnastics hall used for performance and film.
locations.facilities: On-site Lago-Bar for catering; qualified in-house technical staff manage events due to the stage setup and specialised equipment (own site).
locations.logistics: Reachable by tram line 8, highway accessible, large on-site parking lot (own site).

locations.name: Hinterbergwerk
locations.setting: The largest rental studio in Wiesbaden, combining older building character with modern technical fit-out for photo and film production in the Rhine-Main area.

locations.name: Historisches Feuerwehrhaus Ketzerbach
locations.setting: A two storey fire station built in 1911 on Ketzerbach in Marburg's old town, still in use by a volunteer fire brigade unit and keeping vintage engines and equipment on site.

locations.name: Hotel Adlon Kempinski Berlin
locations.setting: A rebuilt grand hotel beside the Brandenburg Gate, with a marble lobby, ballroom and period-style suites used for period and contemporary interiors.
locations.facilities: Two ballrooms and 16 function rooms. Ballroom 500 m2 (500 reception, 340 banquet, 300 classroom); Palais Room 450 m2 (400 reception, 300 banquet, 240 classroom); Event Location 1907, 330 m2 (200 reception, 120 banquet); Large Wintergarten 147 m2 (100 reception, 90 banquet); Academy Rooms 1-2, 120 m2 each (90 reception, 80 banquet, 60 classroom); Bundeszimmer 74 m2 (60 reception, 50 banquet, 42 classroom); smaller rooms range 40 to 84 m2. Most function rooms have natural daylight.

locations.name: Humboldt University of Berlin
locations.setting: Berlin's oldest university on Unter den Linden, with a neoclassical main building, historic lecture halls, a courtyard and library reading rooms in the government district.

locations.name: Hyparschale Magdeburg
locations.setting: A 1969 multi-purpose hall by engineer Ulrich Muther next to Magdeburg's Stadthalle, built from four self-supporting hyperbolic paraboloid concrete shells and reopened in 2024 after restoration.

locations.name: Justizpalast Munich
locations.setting: A neo-baroque courthouse from 1897 housing Munich's higher regional court, with a domed atrium, marble stairways and panelled courtrooms.

locations.name: KaDeWe
locations.setting: One of continental Europe's largest department stores, with Art Deco and postwar interiors, a glass-domed food hall and escalator halls suited to retail and crowd scenes.

locations.name: Kammergericht Berlin
locations.setting: Berlin's highest court, a Wilhelmine-era courthouse with a domed entrance hall, marble staircases and panelled courtrooms.

locations.name: Kampnagel
locations.setting: Former crane factory in Hamburg's Winterhude district converted into a production house for theatre, dance and performance, with large industrial halls and a forecourt.
locations.facilities: During the 2026-2028 renovation, spaces available for hire are Hall k6, Foyer k6, 'Links vorbei', KX (80 seats) and 6a (80 seats); housed in a former factory building (own site).

locations.name: Kap Arkona
locations.setting: Northern tip of Rügen with two historic lighthouses, a former Cold War radar bunker and a reconstructed Slavic hillfort on chalk and boulder-clay cliffs above the Baltic.

locations.name: Kloster Eberbach
locations.setting: Former Cistercian monastery in the Rheingau with a Romanesque basilica, a vaulted dormitory, wine cellars and surrounding vineyards, now run as an events and wine estate.
locations.suitability: The monastery is described as offering interior and exterior filming, suitable for photo shoots, advertising, image videos and TV productions. Spaces named for use include the cloisters, lay refectory, monks' dormitory, baroque floor rooms, basilica, hospital cellar and treasury (own site).

locations.name: Kokerei Hansa
locations.setting: Former coking plant in Dortmund with intact coke oven batteries, coal towers, pump houses and machine halls preserved as an industrial heritage site.
